name: Procurement & Purchasing
tagline: Spend, purchase orders, supplier on-time delivery, lead time, rejections, price variance and contract coverage for buying teams
description: Purchase-order and PO-line exports from ERP and procure-to-pay tools (SAP MM ME2N/ME2M/ME80FN, Oracle Purchasing, Coupa, SAP Ariba, Microsoft Dynamics, NetSuite, Odoo, Zoho Inventory), goods-receipt (GRN, MIGO, MRN) registers, vendor masters, spend-analysis cubes and Indian purchase registers from Tally, Busy and Marg.

fields.label: PO number
fields.description: Identifies each purchase order; repeats on every line of a multi-line PO.

fields.label: Promised / need-by date
fields.description: When the supplier was due to deliver: the line's delivery, need-by or promised date.

fields.label: Supplier rating / score
fields.description: Supplier evaluation or scorecard score; check the scale before comparing.

fields.label: Unit price
fields.description: Price per unit on the order line; never summed, only used to rebuild value.

fields.label: Standard / contract price
fields.description: The price the line is measured against for price variance: standard cost, contract price or last price paid.

fields.label: Days late
fields.description: Days between the promised date and the receipt; zero or negative means on time.

subDomains.name: Purchase orders & PO lines
subDomains.description: One row per purchase order or PO line with supplier, item, quantity, price, value, PO date and the promised delivery date.

subDomains.name: Goods receipts & supplier delivery
subDomains.description: One row per goods receipt (GRN) or received PO line with promised and actual receipt dates and the quantities received, accepted and rejected.

subDomains.name: Supplier master
subDomains.description: One row per supplier with its code, type, location, tax ID, payment terms, status and the date it was onboarded.

subDomains.name: Spend analysis
subDomains.description: One row per spend transaction (a purchase invoice or PO line) with supplier, category, business unit and amount, as in a spend cube or purchase register.

kpis.name: Spend (all lines)
kpis.definition: Value on every line, before removing cancelled orders.
kpis.formula: Σ line value (or quantity × unit price, or invoice amount)

variants.label: Quantity ordered × unit price
variants.caveat: No value column, so spend is quantity ordered × unit price, line by line.

variants.label: Invoice amount
variants.caveat: Spend is taken from invoice amounts, so it counts what was billed rather than what was ordered.

variants.label: Value received
variants.caveat: Only a received-value column is available, so spend counts goods received rather than ordered.

kpis.name: Total spend
kpis.definition: Value purchased in the period, excluding cancelled orders.
kpis.formula: Σ line value (or quantity × unit price), excluding cancelled lines

variants.label: All lines
variants.caveat: No PO status, so spend is taken as recorded; any cancelled orders are included.

pitfalls: Spend lands on the date you analyse by: the PO date shows commitments, the receipt or invoice date shows what was delivered or billed.
Lines in different currencies are added as they stand; convert to one currency before upload.

kpis.name: Purchase orders
kpis.definition: Distinct purchase orders raised in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct PO numbers

variants.label: Row count (no PO number)
variants.caveat: No PO number column, so every row is counted as one order. Check the grain.

kpis.name: Suppliers
kpis.definition: Distinct suppliers on the orders, receipts or invoices in the period; on a supplier master, every listed supplier.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct suppliers
pitfalls: The same supplier spelt two ways counts twice; a supplier code is more reliable than a name.

kpis.name: Average PO value
kpis.definition: Spend per purchase order.
kpis.formula: Total spend ÷ purchase orders
pitfalls: Many small POs push the average down and add processing cost; catalogues or blanket orders usually serve them better.

kpis.name: Supplier on-time delivery
kpis.definition: Share of received lines that arrived by the promised date.
kpis.formula: Lines received on or before the promised date ÷ received lines with a promised date

variants.label: Receipt date on or before the promised date
variants.caveat: Measured on received lines only, so open lines already past their date are not yet counted late.

variants.label: Days late of zero or less

pitfalls: Counted per receipt line, not per PO: one late line in a large order counts once, like any other line.
Companies often allow a grace window (say two days early or late); this measure has none.

kpis.name: Average supplier lead time
kpis.definition: Average days from the purchase order to the goods receipt.
kpis.formula: Average of (receipt date − PO date) in days, over received lines

variants.label: Lead-time column
variants.caveat: Uses the lead-time column as reported; in a supplier or material master it is usually the planned lead time, not the lead time achieved.

pitfalls: Lines not yet received enter the average only once they arrive, so recent periods look faster than they are.

kpis.name: Supplier rejection rate
kpis.definition: Share of received quantity rejected at inspection or returned to the supplier.
kpis.formula: Σ quantity rejected ÷ Σ quantity received

variants.label: (Received − accepted) ÷ received quantity
variants.caveat: No rejected-quantity column, so rejections are received minus accepted quantity.

pitfalls: Quantities in different units (pieces, kg, metres) are added as they stand; compare suppliers within one material or unit.

kpis.name: Goods receipts
kpis.definition: Distinct goods receipts (GRNs) posted in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct GRN numbers

variants.label: Rows with a receipt date
variants.caveat: No GRN number column, so every received line is counted as one receipt.

kpis.name: Spend on contract
kpis.definition: Share of spend placed against a contract or rate agreement.
kpis.formula: Spend with a contract ÷ total spend

variants.label: Lines with a contract reference
variants.caveat: A line counts as on contract when it carries a contract or agreement reference.

pitfalls: Spend with no contract is not always maverick: one-off and low-value buys often have none by design.

kpis.name: Spend per supplier
kpis.definition: Average spend with each supplier used in the period.
kpis.formula: Total spend ÷ suppliers
pitfalls: A long tail of small suppliers pulls the average down; the Pareto chart shows how concentrated spend really is.

kpis.name: Active suppliers %
kpis.definition: Share of suppliers on the master that are active or approved, rather than blocked or inactive.
kpis.formula: Suppliers with an active status ÷ suppliers with a status

variants.label: Active status ÷ suppliers with a status

kpis.name: Average supplier rating
kpis.definition: Average evaluation or scorecard score across rated suppliers.
kpis.formula: Average of supplier rating
pitfalls: Check the scale (out of 5, 10 or 100) and how the score is built before comparing suppliers.

kpis.name: Average credit days
kpis.definition: Average credit period, in days, granted by suppliers.
kpis.formula: Average of credit days
pitfalls: In India, payments to MSME suppliers are due within 45 days whatever the agreed terms (MSMED Act, section 43B(h) of the Income Tax Act).

kpis.name: MSME suppliers %
kpis.definition: Share of suppliers registered as micro, small or medium enterprises.
kpis.formula: MSME suppliers ÷ suppliers with a type

variants.label: MSME type ÷ suppliers with a type

pitfalls: Check which values count as MSME in Check & map › Value meanings.

kpis.name: Open PO value
kpis.definition: Value ordered but not yet delivered.
kpis.formula: Σ value still to be delivered

variants.label: Open quantity × unit price
variants.caveat: Rebuilt line by line from the quantity still to deliver and the unit price.

variants.label: Value of lines not received or cancelled
variants.caveat: No open-quantity column, so lines not yet closed count at full value, including partly received ones.

kpis.name: Quantity received %
kpis.definition: Share of the quantity ordered that has been received so far.
kpis.formula: Σ quantity received ÷ Σ quantity ordered
pitfalls: Recent orders are still being delivered, so recent periods read low until the goods arrive.

kpis.name: Purchase price variance
kpis.definition: Extra paid over the standard or contract price (negative means savings).
kpis.formula: Σ (unit price − standard price) × quantity

variants.label: (Unit price − standard price) × quantity received
variants.caveat: No quantity ordered, so the variance is weighted by the quantity received.

pitfalls: PPV is only as good as the standard it is measured against; a stale standard cost makes every buyer look good or bad.

kpis.name: Price variance %
kpis.definition: Purchase price variance as a share of what the same quantity would cost at the standard price.
kpis.formula: PPV ÷ Σ standard price × quantity, on lines with both prices

variants.label: PPV ÷ standard value, lines with both prices

kpis.name: Requisition-to-PO time
kpis.definition: Average days from the purchase requisition to the purchase order.
kpis.formula: Average of (PO date − requisition date) in days

kpis.name: Late deliveries
kpis.definition: Received lines that arrived after the promised date.
kpis.formula: Count of lines received after the promised date

variants.label: Receipt after the promised date
variants.caveat: Counts received lines only; open lines past their date are not yet counted.

kpis.name: Average days late
kpis.definition: Average days past the promised date, for lines that arrived late.
kpis.formula: Average days late over late lines

variants.label: Receipt − promised date, late lines
variants.caveat: Calendar days between the promised and receipt dates, over lines received after the promised date.

kpis.name: Value received
kpis.definition: Value of goods received in the period.
kpis.formula: Σ received value (or quantity received × unit price)

variants.label: Quantity received × unit price
variants.caveat: No received-value column, so value is quantity received × unit price.

kpis.name: Purchase invoices
kpis.definition: Distinct supplier invoices booked in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct supplier invoice numbers
pitfalls: Invoice numbers are unique per supplier, not across suppliers, so two suppliers' invoice 101 count once.

kpis.name: Spend with a PO
kpis.definition: Share of spend placed against a purchase order rather than bought without one.
kpis.formula: Spend on lines with a PO ÷ total spend

variants.label: Lines with a PO number
variants.caveat: A line counts as on PO when it carries a PO number.

kpis.name: Blocked suppliers
kpis.definition: Suppliers on the master that are blocked, inactive or suspended.
kpis.formula: Distinct suppliers with a blocked or inactive status

kpis.name: Order lines
kpis.definition: Rows in the period: PO lines, receipt lines or spend lines.
kpis.formula: Count of rows

kpis.name: Lines per PO
kpis.definition: Average number of lines on each purchase order.
kpis.formula: Order lines ÷ purchase orders

kpis.name: Tax on purchases
kpis.definition: GST or VAT charged on the purchases in the period.
kpis.formula: Σ tax amount
pitfalls: When IGST, CGST and SGST sit in separate columns only one is mapped here; add the others as column KPIs.

kpis.name: Requesters
kpis.definition: Distinct people who requested purchases in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct requesters

charts.title: Spend over time
charts.reason: Spend per period is a set of discrete totals by PO date, so columns from a zero baseline compare them honestly.

charts.title: Purchase orders over time
charts.reason: A count of orders over time; the line shows the buying rhythm next to the spend columns.

charts.title: Supplier on-time delivery over time
charts.reason: A rate recomputed for each period of promised dates and drawn as a line, never averaged across suppliers.

charts.title: Supplier on-time delivery over time
charts.reason: A rate recomputed for each receipt period and drawn as a line, never averaged across suppliers.

charts.title: Goods receipts over time
charts.reason: Receipts per period are discrete counts, so columns from a zero baseline show the inward workload.

charts.title: Spend over time
charts.reason: Spend per period of invoice date, as columns from a zero baseline so the totals compare honestly.

charts.title: Suppliers onboarded over time
charts.reason: How the supplier base grew: suppliers counted by the period they were onboarded, as columns from zero.

charts.title: Spend by supplier
charts.reason: One measure across many named suppliers: sorted horizontal bars keep the names readable. Top 10 plus Others.

charts.title: Spend by category
charts.reason: Part-to-whole across many categories: a treemap sizes each by spend so the big categories stand out. Top 12 plus Others.

charts.title: Spend by buyer
charts.reason: Who places the spend: sorted bars per buyer or purchasing group, top 12 plus Others.

charts.title: Spend by cost centre
charts.reason: Which parts of the business spend most: sorted bars, top 12 plus Others.

charts.title: Suppliers by type
charts.reason: A handful of supplier types (MSME, large, strategic, import) as parts of the supplier base: a donut shows the split.

charts.title: Suppliers by location
charts.reason: Where the supplier base sits: sorted bars per country, state or city, top 12 plus Others.

charts.title: Suppliers by status
charts.reason: A few statuses (active, blocked, pending) as parts of the master: a donut shows the split at a glance.

charts.title: Supplier concentration (Pareto)
charts.reason: How concentrated spend is: each supplier's share as columns and the cumulative share as a line on one 0–100% axis, so the few suppliers that carry most of the spend stand out.

charts.title: On-time delivery by supplier
charts.reason: A rate compared across suppliers: sorted bars of the recomputed on-time share, with suppliers under 20 lines hidden so a few deliveries do not rank them.

charts.title: Rejection rate by supplier
charts.reason: Which suppliers send the most rejected material: the recomputed rejection rate per supplier, with suppliers under 20 receipt lines hidden.

charts.title: How long suppliers take
charts.reason: Lead times are skewed: a histogram of lines per band of days from PO to receipt shows the long tail an average hides.

charts.title: Days early or late

x.label: Days after the promised date (negative is early)

charts.reason: The spread of arrival against the promised date: lines per band of days early or late, so near misses and very late lines both show.

charts.title: Spend on contract by category
charts.reason: Where buying happens off contract: the recomputed on-contract share per category, with categories under 20 lines hidden.

charts.title: Supplier rating by type
charts.reason: An average score compared across supplier types: sorted bars, with types under 10 suppliers hidden.

charts.title: Credit days by supplier type
charts.reason: Payment terms compared across supplier types, for instance to check MSME suppliers against the 45-day limit.

charts.title: Supplier spend
charts.reason: Several measures per supplier: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

charts.title: Supplier delivery scorecard
charts.reason: Delivery measures per supplier side by side: a sortable table, the usual supplier scorecard.

charts.title: Spend by category and supplier count
charts.reason: Spend, supplier count and spend per supplier per category: shows where the supplier base is fragmented.

pitfalls: Spend lands on the date you analyse by: the PO date shows commitments, the receipt or invoice date shows what was delivered or billed.
Cancelled and rejected orders must be left out of spend; check which statuses count as cancelled in Check & map › Value meanings.
On-time delivery and lead time are measured on received lines only, so orders still open and already late are not yet counted.
Rates such as on-time delivery, rejection and spend on contract are recomputed from totals for every period and group, never averaged across suppliers.
Values in different currencies or quantities in different units are added as they stand; convert or filter to one before comparing.
